transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick roll call — Maya from Redwood, Diego our solutions engineer, Evelyn on customer success.

[00:00:12] Leah (CTO): Hi, Leah here.

[00:00:15] Jordan (Head of Security): Jordan here.

[00:00:18] Samir (DevOps): Samir, yep.

[00:00:21] Maya: Great. The goal for today is just to understand Cedarmark's security decision criteria and what hosting pathways you're considering — hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, or private VPC/on-prem. We'll be pretty pragmatic, lots of clarifying Qs.

[00:00:37] Jordan: Yeah, high level — we run a lot of customer PII for personalization, and compliance is table stakes. SOC2 is yes, but we also need to map to ISO processes for EMEA clients.

[00:00:49] Diego (SE): Understood. Quick question on data flows — do inference requests ever touch long term storage in your pipeline or is it ephemeral logs only?

[00:00:57] Samir: Good Q. We log requests for 7 days to troubleshoot, then we have a longer analytics stream that keeps anonymized aggregates — but some dev teams asked for up to 90 days for replays (internal only). We can scope that.

[00:01:12] Maya: That's useful — helps figure retention and audit log needs. Jordan, for SOC2/ISO, are you focused on "we must have provider SOC2" or "we can accept equivalent controls with attestation"?

[00:01:22] Jordan: We prefer a SOC2 Type II report and evidence of ongoing ISO alignment. If Redwood has SOC2 and ISO docs, that covers majority of procurement red flags. Also will want detailed answers on encryption and KMS — we have a BYOK preference for sensitive models.

[00:01:38] Evelyn (CSM): We can share the SOC2 pack and ISO alignment spreadsheet. I'll attach the artifact links right after the call.

[00:01:46] Leah: Another angle: latency. Our checkout flows need sub-300ms in 95th percentile for the concierge suggestions. If hosted adds jitter we may need Dedicated.

[00:01:58] Diego: Good to call that out. We can run a Dedicated baseline on your traffic profile. Hosted typically hits low latency, but dedicated lets you pin GPUs and set throughput guarantees — tradeoff is cost and setup time.

[00:02:12] Jordan: From security side, questions: SSO/SAML support, SCIM for user provisioning, RBAC scoping between teams, and audit logs with retention control.

[00:02:22] Maya: Yep. Redwood supports SAML 2.0, SCIM for user sync, and RBAC at token and project level. We also expose audit logs — there's an event stream that can be pushed to S3 or to your SIEM. Diego, do you want to add detail on the audit exports?

[00:02:34] Diego: Sure — audit events include token creation, model rollouts, API key usage, admin actions. We offerExports to S3 or to your logging endpoint (syslog/HTTP). Retention is configurable on Dedicated/Private; hosted has a default 30-day retention with add-on retention packages.

[00:02:50] Jordan: 30 days is low for us — we need 365 days for certain markets, and we log at higher fidelity for admin actions. Can Hosted be extended?

[00:02:58] Maya: Yes, through our add-on you can extend retention, or use Dedicated/Private where you control the retention window. We'll include pricing delta in the follow-up.

[00:03:06] Samir: On KMS — we use AWS KMS today and we have a preference for BYOK where customer keys never leave our tenancy. How does Redwood handle BYOK?

[00:03:14] Diego: We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS for hosted and a bring-your-own-HSM option for Private. For Hosted BYOK, we integrate with your KMS using a cross-account role so keys remain in your AWS account — cryptographic operations are performed without Redwood holding plaintext keys. There are some constraints for cross-region keys, we can document that.

[00:03:32] Jordan: Cross-account roles sounds promising but we need the exact flow and proof that keys are never exported.

[00:03:38] Maya: We'll attach the KMS topology diagram and the whitepaper on BYOK — Diego will flag the limitations (e.g., certain TPU/backends can't use external HSMs).

[00:03:45] Leah: Also, model artifacts — where are KV caches and model weights stored? We need to ensure model weights never persist to our S3 buckets unless we explicitly request model checkpoint export.

[00:03:56] Diego: Good call. Model weights are stored in Redwood-managed storage for Hosted/Dedicated. For Private you can opt to host weights in your environment. KV cache is ephemeral, but we do offer optional prefix cache snapshots for performance; those are encrypted at rest. We can make sure snapshot exports are disabled by default.

[00:04:15] Jordan: Okay. On RBAC — we need per-team isolation and ability to rotate keys per service. Does Redwood support token scoping and granular roles?

[00:04:24] Maya: Yes, token scoping, role-based roles (sorry) — RBAC with pre-defined roles and custom roles. Tokens can be scoped to projects and routes; rotation APIs exist and we recommend short-lived tokens for services.

[00:04:35] Jordan: When you say "audit events" — is that tamper-evident? We need to forward logs to our immutability store.

[00:04:41] Diego: We support signed audit logs when you integrate via log shipping — we can sign events and you can push to your append-only store. Private deployment can mount a write-once S3 bucket or a Vault-backed immutable persistence for logs.

[00:04:55] Samir: Can we get sample event schema? That helps our SIEM mapping.

[00:04:59] Maya: We'll include a sample event schema in the follow-up — JSON with timestamp, actor, action, resource, request_id, and optional payload hash.

[00:05:08] Leah: About network: for Private we'd want VPC peering and no public egress for inference calls. For Dedicated, is there a VPC option?

[00:05:17] Diego: Dedicated can be provisioned with customer VPC endpoints (VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on region). Private is fully customer-managed. Hosted uses TLS-only public endpoints by default — we can provide private connectivity via PrivateLink in selected clouds.

[00:05:29] Jordan: Great. On compliance artifacts — will we get the full SOC2 report or a redacted summary? Procurement will need both redacted and full under NDA.

[00:05:37] Evelyn: We typically share a redacted SOC2 publicly and provide full under NDA. We'll send the redacted pack now and a link to request the full version.

[00:05:45] Samir: Side note — do you do model evaluation / data leakage monitoring? We have concerns about PII regeneration in model outputs.

[00:05:52] Diego: We have a quality-monitoring tool that can run prompt sets and flag PII exposures; Redwood Optimize has evals and regression alerts — we can plug your test prompts and run a small eval. Also prefix caching reduces leakage surface for shared prompts, but we'll need to talk specifics.

[00:06:07] Jordan: That sounds helpful. For procurement we also need SLAs — uptime and latency SLOs, especially if we go Dedicated.

[00:06:13] Maya: Hosted SLA is our standard SLO for API availability; Dedicated comes with an SLA you can negotiate in contract (higher uptime and latency commitments). We'll add sample SLA language to the package.

[00:06:23] Leah: Time-to-provision — how long to stand up Dedicated vs Private?

[00:06:27] Diego: Dedicated typically 2–4 weeks depending on capacity and region; Private can be 4–8+ weeks for on-prem integrations because of network and HSM work. Hosted is immediate.

[00:06:36] Jordan: What about data residency? Some EU customers require data to remain in EU. Does Redwood guarantee region-specific processing?

[00:06:42] Maya: Yes, region pinning is supported on Dedicated and Private. Hosted can be region restricted for larger contracts; we do have hosted regions in EU and NA. We'll share the region availability matrix.

[00:06:52] Samir: Security test question — do you allow pentests or do you have a bug bounty program?

[00:06:57] Diego: We allow scheduled pentests for Dedicated/Private with scoping rules; for Hosted we have an authorized pentest program and also a public bug bounty on the platform surface. We'll share the policies.

[00:07:08] Jordan: Good. Cost tradeoffs — Leah mentioned sub-300ms need. What's a rough delta for Dedicated vs Hosted for that SLA?

[00:07:15] Diego: Roughly, Dedicated can reduce variance and hit lower p99s because you're not contending with noisy neighbors — cost delta depends on model size and quantization. We'll run the demo with your sample traffic and give numbers; for many workloads Dedicated increases fixed cost but reduces per-token variance and can be cheaper at high throughput.

[00:07:31] Maya: Also, we offer Optimize recommendations — quantization and batching settings that can reduce per-token cost while keeping latency constraints.

[00:07:37] Leah: Perfect. Okay, procurement will also ask about backup and retention for logs and keys. Do you provide key rotation automation?

[00:07:45] Diego: Yes, rotation APIs and integration with your KMS rotation policies. For BYOK we recommend rotating the envelope keys and keeping a clear rotation cadence; we can demonstrate automation.

[00:07:56] Jordan: One smaller nit — admin access and separation of duties. We want at least two-person approval for critical actions (e.g., model rollout to prod). Does Redwood support approval flows?

[00:08:04] Maya: Yes we do workflows for rollouts: approvals, canary windows, and automatic rollback. We can also integrate with your ticketing system for approval gating.

[00:08:11] Samir: For the Dedicated demo, can we include a simulated canary and a rollback to see the audit trail?

[00:08:16] Diego: Absolutely — we'll include a canary demo and show event logs and signed audit trail.

[00:08:20] Leah: Great. Anything else on retention? Our legal team wants retention by data type: PII requests retained for 365 days, non-PII analytics for 5 years aggregated only.

[00:08:31] Maya: That can be configured — Hosted with retention add-on or Dedicated/Private where you control the storage lifecycle. We'll include config examples for lifecycle rules on S3.

[00:08:40] Jordan: One more — vulnerability disclosure for model updates, and how you handle dependency CVEs in the runtime.

[00:08:47] Diego: We have a vulnerability management program and we publish CVE response timelines for critical issues. For Dedicated we can coordinate maintenance windows for kernel/driver updates.

[00:08:57] Maya: Okay — looks like we have a clear set of asks. We'll follow up with: SOC2 + ISO artifacts, KMS/BYOK topology diagram, sample audit event schema, SSO/SAML integration guide, Dedicated demo invite, and rough pricing differential.

[00:09:12] Leah: That sounds good. Quick timelines — can we get the artifacts by Tuesday? That would help legal move fast.

[00:09:18] Maya: We'll get the redacted SOC2 and the SSO guide by Tuesday (2026-08-18). Diego will schedule the Dedicated demo for the week of 2026-08-24.

[00:09:26] Jordan: Thanks, appreciate it.

[00:09:28] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll send a short recap and action items.

[00:09:33] (call ends)
